title.narrative: Ministry of Finance: Human Resources for Health Salary Support Activity (Government-to Government)

description.narrative: (Malawi): The shortage and equitable distribution of well-trained, and highly skilled health care workers is the most significant barrier to ensuring universal health coverage and improving the health status of Malawians. In line with USAID's vision of systems strengthening for greater sustainability and resilience, USAID entered into a direct government to government agreement with two district councils (Zomba and Mangochi), to strengthen health systems. Given the pivotal role of human resources to obtain the expected outcomes, and the acute shortage of healthcare workers in the districts, USAID is providing direct funding to enable the Ministry of Finance pay the salaries of one hundred and fifty one health care workers and four support staff recruited under the Zomba District Council including two hundred and thirty one health care workers and one support staff for Mangochi District Council. At the end of the three-year period, the Government of Malawi will take over payment of salaries. Funding for the salaries passes through the national payroll system with USAID resources managed in a separate account. FY 2022 funds will enable the Ministry of Finance to continue to provide salary payment for health care workers and support staff recruited by the two District Councils. . ..This activity leverages PEPFAR funding, which has successfully transitioned U.S. government funded health care workers to the Government of Malawi. The use of the government's payroll systems generates commitment and accountability in support of locally led development..This activity supports the Integrated Country Strategy Mission Objective 1.2 - Public service providers improve the integrity and quality of public services, particularly those supported with U.S. foreign assistance and 3.2 - Malawi improves access to and quality of health services so that more of its citizens gain and retain full health and are able to contribute productively at home, in the community, and at work.
